title: Drives That Hurt
aim: Drive with control at well under full power, aim it low at your opponent's backhand or feet, and follow a good drive or swing in to the net.

stages.title: Serve, Return, Drive, Counter
stages.inShort: A serves and drives down the line, B returns, runs across to the kitchen and counters the drive.
rules: A serves cross-court from the right half (right as you face the net): into the back third, angled to B's forehand near the sideline, well over the net.
B returns back toward A, near the sideline, high enough to give you time. Then B runs diagonally across to the other side of the kitchen line.
A drives (a hard, flat shot) straight down the line at B's backhand. Only 40–60% power, 15–50 cm over the net.
B split-steps (a small hop that lands just as A hits), then counters with a short two-handed backhand (lefties: forehand), down toward the floor and deep.
Stop after the counter and start again. Build it up: serve and return only until steady, then add the drive, then the counter. No points.
stages.tooEasy: Play the full chain each time and count clean chains out of 10. Then serve from the left half.
stages.tooHard: B returns to the middle and runs to the middle of the kitchen line, and A drives down the middle. Less running.
stages.goodLooksLike: 7 out of 10 chains with all four shots clean: serve deep near the sideline, return near the sideline, drive at the backhand low over the net, counter down and deep.

drill.title: First Four Shots — Down-the-Line Drive Chain (Worst-Case Reps)

stages.title: The 60% Drive
stages.inShort: B hits a compact drive at 60% power to the cones at A's feet, then runs in. A says how it arrived.
rules: Put two cones (or bottles) about 1.2–1.5 m behind the kitchen line on A's side. A stands there, like an opponent who has not reached the net yet.
From the baseline, B plays a hybrid drive: a compact swing at about 60% power, aimed at the cones, so it arrives at A's ankles.
A tries to return it and tells B: good ankle height, too high or too fast.
B runs in to the net right behind the hybrid drive.
stages.tooEasy: A moves sideways while B hits. B has to place the hybrid drive where A is moving to, or behind A.
stages.tooHard: B stays at the baseline and works only on the 60% swing and the ankle height, without running in.
stages.goodLooksLike: Every ball arrives low at A's ankles, not at the body, and B is already moving in as it lands.

stages.title: Swing and Charge
stages.inShort: From mid-court, A swings at every ball above the waist and charges the net. Low balls get a soft reset instead.
rules: A and B both start at mid-court (halfway between baseline and kitchen line).
A starts the ball at about half pace to B, then plays B's reply.
Ball above A's waist: A hits a swinging volley (a full swing at the ball before it bounces) and charges the net behind it.
Ball too low, below the net: A does not force it and plays a reset (a soft ball that drops into the kitchen). That is the right answer, not a mistake.
As soon as B has hit the first ball, B also moves forward. From there, play the point out, any shot allowed. No points yet.
stages.tooEasy: Keep score, first to 7. Whoever loses the point starts the next ball.
stages.tooHard: No live point: B just sends A balls, and A only practises the swing and the run to the net.
stages.goodLooksLike: A brushes up the back of the ball, hits it out in front and finishes short, ready for the counter.
